summary: The bill creates a 5-year competitive grant pilot program, funded at up to $500,000 per award with a 25% match, to help child care providers expand or launch programs serving parents who work evenings, nights, or weekends.

scores.thoughts: The bill establishes a new Child Care and Development Innovation Fund and authorizes competitive grants (minimum $25k, maximum $500k per grant) for 5-year periods to expand after-hours child care capacity. It reserves up to 0.25% of annual appropriations under the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act for fiscal years 2027-2031. This directly creates new federal spending authority and outlays.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue measures.
The bill addresses child care access and has no provisions concerning health insurance, medical services, or healthcare delivery systems.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration policy, visas, border enforcement, or immigrant eligibility.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions concern military or defense spending or policy.
No provisions address environmental regulations, climate policy, or conservation.

The bill expands subsidized child care services specifically for working parents (including nontraditional hours) through new federal grants under the Child Care and Development Block Grant framework. This constitutes an expansion of a social support program that helps low- and moderate-income families maintain workforce attachment.

While the bill funds child care programs that may have early childhood development components, it does not engage with K-12 public schools, school choice mechanisms, or federal education policy as defined by the topic criteria.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance abuse policy.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The bill authorizes new mandatory-style grant spending without any offsetting revenue or cuts, thereby increasing the deficit in the near term.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions address voting access, election administration, or voter ID.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill supports workforce participation through child care but does not alter labor law, union rights, collective bargaining, or employer obligations.
No provisions address religious exemptions, anti-discrimination rules, or conflicts between civil rights and religious liberty.
